primary_meaning: The covenant people of God, fulfilled or continued as the Christian Church (spiritual/new Israel)
primary_basis: Hosea 1:10 / 2:23 (applied to Gentile believers in Romans 9:25-26 and 1 Peter 2:10)

alternatives.meaning: The ethnic/physical descendants of Jacob (the Jewish people) remaining distinct as God's chosen people
basis: OT covenant promises taken as irrevocable to ethnic Israel

alternatives.meaning: Jesus Christ himself as the true/faithful Israel in whom the nation's vocation is fulfilled
basis: Isaiah servant songs applied to Christ

alternatives.meaning: The modern geopolitical State of Israel as prophetic fulfillment
All true believers (Jew and Gentile) without strong ecclesiological identification as 'Church as Israel'

notes: Christian interpretation of 'Israel' is sharply divided along theological lines (covenant theology/supersessionism vs. dispensationalism vs. dual-covenant views). The Church-as-true-Israel reading has deep roots in patristic, medieval, Reformation, and much mainline teaching and remains widely recognizable as the historic symbolic default, yet competing literal-ethnic and Christological readings are also longstanding and currently influential; no single symbolic sense commands universal agreement.
